items.title: Saudi-Houthi escalation threatens alternative Red Sea export corridor
items.summary: Saudi-led forces struck Yemen's Hodeidah port after Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports. Saudi Arabia has used western export terminals and its East-West pipeline to mitigate Hormuz disruptions. Oil fell as surplus expectations outweighed the new risk. No incremental crude-export volume loss has been independently established.

observations.label: November 25 escalation
observations.value: Reuters and WSJ report Saudi coalition action at Hodeidah after Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports; threats do not establish port closures.

observations.label: Physical-flow assessment
observations.value: Saudi western ports and East-West pipeline provide an alternate export corridor; no new quantified cargo or export loss independently established.

observations.label: Advisories and next indicators
observations.value: MARAD active advisories unchanged; UKMTO dynamic register did not load incident list. Watch terminal operations, verified loadings, pipeline throughput, insurance, EIA at 10:30 AM ET and OPEC+ Nov 29.

items.key_finding: Red Sea escalation exposes an alternate oil export corridor while market prices continue to reflect expectations of surplus supply.

sources.title: Reuters: Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports and coalition strikes Hodeidah
WSJ: oil prices and renewed Middle East tensions

items.title: Asian chip-heavy equity markets close sharply lower as relief rally fades
items.summary: South Korea erased Tuesday's recovery and Taiwan suffered broad losses as semiconductor selling intensified. Japan also declined while Australia gained. Foreign selling and reported prospective U.S. tariffs compound AI valuation concerns, but the market action does not establish declining semiconductor orders.

observations.label: November 25 local-market closing changes, independently corroborated
observations.value: KOSPI -6.16% to 4,697.51 (MoneyToday and Seoul Market Wire); TAIEX -4.80% to 38,195.43 (CNA and Financial Express); Nikkei -2.78% (SquawkNews and AP, rounded -2.8%).

observations.label: Taiwan breadth and foreign flows, CNA
observations.value: 39 advancers, 1,053 decliners; foreign institutions net sold NT$123.65 billion.

observations.label: Fundamentals and next indicators
observations.value: Price stress reflects AI valuation, trade and liquidity risks, not demonstrated chip-order deterioration. Watch foreign flows, breadth, company order revisions, tariffs, PCE and Treasury yields. Sustained broad recovery would weaken stress signal.

items.key_finding: Asian closing figures confirm the semiconductor-led reversal spread beyond early Tokyo trading.

sources.title: Seoul Market Wire: Korea close and foreign flows
Focus Taiwan: foreign selling and chip moves

items.title: Reports of imminent Section 301 tariff findings add manufacturing supply-chain risk
items.summary: Reuters and Associated Press independently report preparations for additional U.S. tariffs following an industrial overcapacity investigation. USTR documents the original investigation covering major Asian, European and North American trading partners. Rates, product coverage and implementation timing are not yet confirmed.

observations.label: Official scope
observations.value: USTR March 11 initiated Section 301 investigations covering 16 economies including China, Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Mexico and EU.

observations.label: November 25 reporting
observations.value: Reuters and AP cite people familiar with preparations for additional duties; no final rates or effective dates independently established.

observations.label: Market context
observations.value: November 25 Asian closes: KOSPI -6.16%, TAIEX -4.80%, Nikkei approximately -2.8%; tariff reports are one of several catalysts, not sole cause.

observations.label: Next indicators and invalidation
observations.value: Official findings, tariff schedules, exclusions, effective dates, supplier cost pass-through and corporate margin guidance. Delays or broad exclusions would reduce near-term risk.

items.key_finding: Prospective additional duties represent a meaningful but not yet implemented manufacturing cost risk.

sources.title: Reuters: tariff preparations via Korea Times

items.title: Workday falls after hours as subscription-growth guidance tempers earnings beat
items.summary: Workday's earnings beat and growing AI contract value were overshadowed by softer near-term subscription guidance. Shares fell sharply in extended trading. Cash generation and profitability remain strong, but slowing contracted revenue growth warrants monitoring.

observations.label: Extended-hours price observation Nov 24 at 6:30 PM EST
observations.value: WiseView reports $164.50, -8.22% versus regular-session reference of $179.23; Investing.com reported -7.9% at 5:58 PM. Indicative extended-hours prices, not confirmed closing data.

observations.label: Official earnings disclosure
observations.value: Q3 total revenue $2.705B +11.2%, subscription revenue +12.8%, free cash flow $691M vs $550M, non-GAAP operating margin 31.4%; total subscription backlog +6.1%.

observations.label: Forward guidance
observations.value: Q4 subscription revenue approximately $2.6B, +10%, versus 12.8% growth in Q3; near-term forecast slightly below analyst consensus.

observations.label: Risk and next indicators
observations.value: Customer renewals, AI contract conversion, subscription backlog, margins and next regular-session price; reacceleration in subscription growth would weaken the slowdown concern.

items.key_finding: A substantial extended-hours decline contrasts with strong cash generation, but softer subscription guidance is a real fundamental risk.

sources.title: WiseView November 24 6:30 PM ET market snapshot

items.title: Separate vessel-tracking sources indicate severe Hormuz traffic restrictions
items.summary: MarineTraffic figures reported on November 24 indicate a substantial decline in weekly vessel crossings. A separate AIS tracker also shows depressed commercial transits. The data support transportation disruption but do not quantify incremental crude export losses; vessels without AIS and differing coverage limit comparison.

observations.label: MarineTraffic counts reported Nov 24
observations.value: 226 vessels Nov 1–7 versus 125 Nov 17–23, a 44.7% decline; reported by UOL.

observations.label: Separate AIS tracking snapshot Nov 24, 11:51 AM EST
observations.value: hormuz.now reports 7.4 commercial crossings/day over seven days and 2 in the prior 24 hours; differing coverage prevents direct comparison with MarineTraffic.

observations.label: Physical oil-flow assessment
observations.value: Restricted vessel movement is corroborated; incremental crude cargo volume loss and Strait-wide closure are not established.

observations.label: Next indicators
observations.value: Tanker loadings, alternative pipeline volumes, insurance, EIA Nov 25, OPEC+ Nov 29; sustained traffic recovery would weaken the disruption signal.

items.key_finding: Independent tracking indicates severe transportation disruption, but vessel counts cannot be translated directly into barrels of lost supply.
